cases.title: Repo with documented manual processes and missing scripts
cases.user_request: Find automation opportunities in this repo. Look for manual deploy steps, missing setup scripts, repetitive workflows, and things that should be in source control.

notes: The README has a 10-step manual deploy process.
Getting started requires 8 manual commands with no bootstrap script.
Releases are done by manually editing version numbers and creating tags.
The README references a .env.example that does not exist in the repo.
There is a basic CI pipeline but it only runs tests, not deploys.
available_artifacts: README.md with deploy and setup instructions

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with summary, categorized findings, ROI ranking, and quick wins
Each finding includes location, description, impact, effort, and suggested approach
Missing .env.example is flagged with reference to where it is mentioned
Existing CI pipeline is acknowledged, not re-recommended
static_checks: Report has sections for summary, categorized findings, ROI ranking, and quick wins
At least one finding references the README deploy steps
Existing CI pipeline is mentioned as already in place
review_questions: Does each finding cite a specific file and section rather than giving generic advice?
Are the suggested automation approaches concrete enough to act on (naming tools or script types)?

cases.title: Well-automated repo to test false positive rate
cases.user_request: Run the monthly automation opportunities audit. This repo has good CI/CD and scripts already.

notes: The repo has a comprehensive CI/CD pipeline covering test, build, and deploy.
A bootstrap script handles local setup.
There may be a few remaining manual steps in edge cases.
.env.example and all config templates are checked in.
available_artifacts: README.md with setup instructions pointing to bootstrap script
scripts/ directory with setup, deploy, and release scripts

artifact_requirements: Report acknowledges the repo's automation maturity
Few or no false positives recommending automation that already exists
Any findings are genuinely incremental improvements, not basics
Summary honestly reflects the mature state
static_checks: Existing scripts and CI pipelines are acknowledged
Report does not recommend creating automation that already exists
review_questions: Does the report avoid recommending automation that already exists in the repo?
Are the remaining findings genuinely incremental improvements worth the effort?

cases.title: New project with no CI, no scripts, manual everything
cases.user_request: Audit this new project for automation opportunities. We have nothing automated yet and want to know where to start.

notes: This is a new project with source code but no CI/CD pipeline.
The README has manual setup, build, test, and deploy instructions.
There are no scripts, no Makefile, no Dockerfile.
Several source file comments reference config files and env vars that are not in the repo.
The team wants to prioritize the highest-ROI automation first.
available_artifacts: no CI config, no scripts directory

artifact_requirements: Report covers all major automation gaps without being overwhelming
ROI ranking clearly identifies the first 3 things to automate
Quick wins focus on the highest-leverage starting points
Missing artifacts checklist identifies config and env files to add
static_checks: ROI ranking section is present with clear top priorities
Quick wins section identifies 3-5 starting points
Findings reference specific README sections or source file comments
review_questions: Does the ROI ranking help a team decide what to automate first?
Are the quick wins genuinely the highest-leverage starting points for a greenfield project?
